### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleActionsRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ba52069197858607f27ffd8a63b8921e06fd6cc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e1534a2be035094a48558f6472d240d7af6cdd7` — the merge of head `095db1e91fa96a6e947b5e99b1efcc7f23bfd55f` into base `3ba52069197858607f27ffd8a63b8921e06fd6cc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e1534a2be035094a48558f6472d240d7af6cdd7 && git checkout 2e1534a2be035094a48558f6472d240d7af6cdd7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3ba52069197858607f27ffd8a63b8921e06fd6cc 095db1e91fa96a6e947b5e99b1efcc7f23bfd55f && git checkout -B drift-repro 3ba52069197858607f27ffd8a63b8921e06fd6cc && git merge --no-ff 095db1e91fa96a6e947b5e99b1efcc7f23bfd55f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ba52069197858607f27ffd8a63b8921e06fd6cc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3ba52069197858607f27ffd8a63b8921e06fd6cc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `095db1e91fa96a6e947b5e99b1efcc7f23bfd55f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/action-invocation-audit.ts (`ActionInvocationAuditEvent.target` / `.forwardedFrom`, the `metadata.target` write on `branch: 'api'` only, `metadata.forwarded_from`), packages/runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.ts (the runtime event's two members, `actionInvocationTarget`, `actionInvocationForwardedFrom`, `ACTION_FORWARD_MARK_MAX_LENGTH`, the header prose), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (the REST door's two reads), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (the one `target` line in `invokeBusinessAction`), the two test files, .changeset/28281-forwarded-action-audit-rows.md

Inputs: card #28281 (the outer row carries the declared `api` target, the inner REST door records the forward mark as `forwarded_from`, a hint not a surface, one pin on an MCP to api to action-route forward; the seat's claim 6541190282 and its amendment 6541778957 correcting Clause-② to yes and widening the file surface; triage's retriage answer 6541948513: stays `domain:server`, reviewed at this tier; the REWORK asking a shape bound on `forwarded_from`), PR #28389 (body with the two keys and the acceptance notes, the hand-off 6542171435 naming the declaration of record `Clause-②: yes (widening)` since the body's first line cannot be rewritten through the relay, the file list of 7 files, the diff of 283 lines against `main` read whole, 3 commits from the merge-base), the 53 check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-31T10:47Z: all 53 runs completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Build Core, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Auto Label, Build & E2E UI, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test UI (matrix shard/16), Type Check UI, UI Published Artifacts), and the tree at this head for `forwardApiAction` in `action-execution.ts` (the forwarding door writes the mark as `${mark.objectName}/${mark.actionName}`, the object segment being `GLOBAL_ACTION_OBJECT_KEY` = `global` for an object-less action), the inner door's existing loop-refusal read of the same header, `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` in `packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts`, `plugin-audit`'s `index.ts` (it exports `ActionInvocationAuditEvent`) and its `nonEmpty` helper. The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main`; none of this PR's files moved on `main` since the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The two rows now name each other, by declaration not by time** - right. The outer row's `metadata.target` is the action's declared `target` string, produced by `actionInvocationTarget` only when the branch is `api`, from both doors (the MCP `run_action` literal in `invokeBusinessAction` and the REST door). It is the declaration, not the interpolated path, so no caller param reaches the ledger through it, consistent with the row recording no params. The inner row's `metadata.forwarded_from` is the mark the forwarding door set, read from the same header the inner door already reads for its loop refusal.
- **The hint is bounded to the forwarding door's own shape** - right, and it answers the seat's REWORK. The header is caller text bound for the compliance ledger, so `actionInvocationForwardedFrom` records it only when it is two segments joined by one slash, each a `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` machine name (which admits `global`, the object segment the forwarding door writes for an object-less action), at most 255 characters; anything else is left out and the call is answered as before. Never a refusal: the mark gates nothing here, and the inner row's `surface: 'rest'` stays the door's own, so a forged mark mislabels this one key and nothing else.
- **Old rows and non-forward calls are unchanged** - right. `buildActionInvocationAuditRow` writes `target` only on `branch: 'api'` and only when non-empty, and `forwarded_from` only when a conforming mark was carried; a direct call names neither (pinned), and an event that sets neither writes the same row as before.
- **The widening is what the declaration of record says** - right. `ActionInvocationAuditEvent`, exported by `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, gains two optional members; the runtime's event type and helpers are internal to `@objectstack/runtime`. No spec path, no accept set, no stored shape, no route or error code moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. The PR body's `Clause-②: no` is a relay artefact the hand-off explains; the changeset at this head and the claim amendment carry `yes (widening)`, and this record reads that as the declaration.
- **Pins hold both ways** - right. The runtime test routes the forward into the real REST door with the headers `forwardApiAction` sends, so the inner row is written by the door reading the mark as on a server: MCP and REST forwards name the pair, a direct call names neither, the declaration not the interpolated path, the forged mark on a direct call; plugin-audit reads the pair back through a real engine and refuses `target` on a non-api branch. Four ablations each red the cases they should and are restored byte-identical.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch** - accepted. Two optional members on an exported event type and two optional keys in an audit row's `metadata`, with every existing row and call unchanged; no protocol surface moves, so `patch` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right pair.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The PR body's declaration line** - reads `Clause-②: no` and cannot be edited through the relay (its first line is the attribution, not a signature). The landing stroke should cite this record and the changeset as the declaration of record, as the hand-off does; if a body edit by hand is cheap for the seat, it removes the mismatch for later readers.
- **Only the REST door records `forwardedFrom`** - as the card asks; the MCP door reads no mark, and a forward whose target is `/mcp` itself is unmeasured and left as it was. Not owed.
- **The S2 latency note on the card** - untouched, as dispatched.
- **The seat lands** - no Tier H path (no `docs/adr`, no `skills/**`, 283 lines), no human gate; no name approval owed (audit-row metadata keys, no spec key).

### ④ Design judgment

- Tried: a mark of `global/send_digest` (admitted, as the forwarding door writes it for an object-less action); a mark with a leading slash or three segments (left out, the call unchanged); a `target` declared with a template hole (recorded as declared, the hole unfilled, which is the point); an api action whose `target` is an external URL (recorded as declared on the outer row, no inner row exists, nothing joins, nothing wrong). Keying the hint's admission off the same identifier grammar the declarations are held to is what keeps caller text out of the ledger without inventing a second grammar. Nothing to add.

**Verdict reasoning.** The outer row names the declared target on the api branch only, the inner row names the forward mark it arrived carrying and only in the shape the forwarding door writes, every other row and answer is unchanged, the hint is a hint and the surface stays the door's own, the widening is two optional members on one exported type declared in the changeset and the claim, the patch level is right, the pins run the real inner door and hold both ways, and every check on this head is green or skipped.
